newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold ends down, silver up on better supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold ends down, silver up on better supply.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closes 15 rupees lower at 4,795 rupees per 10 gramme, demand resistance caps gains while moderate losses in the world market prompts profit-taking.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) close 200 rupees lower at 56,100 rupees per piece.
** Silver (.999) closes 10 rupees higher at 7,030 rupees per kg, fresh arrivals trim early gains.
Gold 24 carat ended Thursday 15 rupees lower at 4,795 rupees per 10 gramme on demand resistance at higher levels and profit-taking, dealers said.
They said a subdued trend in world markets also dragged prices lower towards close after weak early trade. Gold supplies were at a low level on Thursday and trade poor, dealers said.
Gold was up 30 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) closed 200 rupees lower at 56,100 rupees per piece.
They were up 400 rupees per piece on Wednesday after gaining 1,100 rupees last week.
Silver (.999) closed 10 rupees higher at 7,030 rupees per kg but down 5 rupees from the day's opening as fresh arrivals trimmed early gains towards close, dealers said.
Silver was down 20 rupees per kg on Wednesday.
"Actually market opened firm today on limited inflows but gradually arrivals improved and ...(market) lost early steam," one dealer said.
